A compliance release. No tool changes anything it did not change before, and no
tool returns anything different: what changed is what the server and the bundle
say about themselves, which is what the MCP Directory reads when reviewing a
submission.

## The server never sent its tool annotations

`tools.ts` has always carried a `title` and a `readOnlyHint` or `destructiveHint`
for every tool. The `tools/list` handler dropped both, returning only name,
description and input schema — so every client, the directory included, saw 109
tools with no title and no safety hint.

Every tool now sends:

- `title`, the human-readable name it already had
- `readOnlyHint` for the 83 tools that only read, `destructiveHint` for the 26
  that write
- `openWorldHint`, since each one reaches `connect.garmin.com`

`setup_credentials` was the only tool declaring neither hint. It overwrites
stored credentials and the OAuth tokens of the previous session, so it now
declares `destructiveHint` alongside the confirmation it already required.

## The password could reach the log

With `DEBUG_GARMIN` set, tool arguments were written to stderr in full. For
`setup_credentials` that meant the Garmin password in clear text, three lines
below a comment promising it would never be logged.

Sensitive values are now replaced with `[redacted]` and the email is masked
before anything is written. Nothing is logged at all without `DEBUG_GARMIN`, as
before.

## Manifest

| Field | Change |
|---|---|
| `display_name` | Added — it is required, and its absence blocked validation. Reads "Garmin Connect" |
| `icon` | Was `.\GARMIN.png`, a Windows-style path that does not resolve when the bundle is unpacked elsewhere. Now `GARMIN.png`, and the image is square at 512×512, the size Claude Desktop asks for |
| `privacy_policies` | Added — a missing privacy policy is an immediate rejection. Lists this project's policy and Garmin's |
| `tools` | All 109 declared, generated from the source by `npm run sync:manifest` and verified in CI so the list cannot drift from the server |
| `long_description`, `keywords`, `compatibility` | Added for the directory listing, and to state the platforms and Node version required |

The MCP handshake had been introducing the server as `garmin-mcp 1.0.0` since
v1. It now reports its real name and version, checked against `package.json` and
`manifest.json` by the same script that syncs the tool list.

## Release process

The bundle and its checksum are built from the tag by a GitHub Actions workflow,
with production dependencies only, rather than packed by hand — which is how
v4.3.1 came to exist in the manifest while the published bundle was still
v4.3.0. The README download links point at `releases/latest` and stop drifting
with each version.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. If you are upgrading, reinstall the bundle and restart
Claude Desktop: the extension runs from its installed copy, so a restart alone
keeps the previous build.

Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

Expected digest:

```
6b6f3bd1c77a50daf62b833094b65ce6f2c5e708a76988d487b87dde57da9326
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.3.0...v4.3.1
